images.prompt: Photorealistic macro photograph of a handcrafted miniature tabletop diorama. A compact graphite router about the size of a paperback stands at the left of a pale neutral tabletop, its brushed top vented and its two short antennas chamfered. From it, three flat frosted acrylic signal rings of increasing size lie concentrically across the tabletop, each glowing softly at its milky edge. Within the rings sits a grid of six small ivory card desks, each with a tiny graphite laptop lit by a faint frosted screen. In the far right corner, one desk sits just outside the outer ring, and its laptop's single acid-lime indicator light is the only one still searching. Dust sits lightly on the rings, and fine fibres show at the desk edges. The layout is even. Wide 16:9 landscape frame. The hero object sits slightly left of centre on the lower third, with the related objects extending to the right so the workflow reads left to right. Clean, generous negative space above. Shot as a real physical model, not a 3D render. Materials are limited and tactile: heavyweight ivory cotton paper and card with visible fibres, soft folds and slightly deckled edges; matte, bead-blasted graphite metal with fine machining lines, chamfered edges and tiny hex fasteners; frosted acrylic with milky edges and a soft internal glow; sandblasted frosted glass. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface. Colour palette is restrained and nearly monochrome: white #FFFFFF, warm ivory, pale neutral #F3F5F2, soft grey-green #DCE1DA, muted graphite #626A64 and deep graphite #191D1B. Acid lime #D0F344 appears only on the lime element named in the scene, as the single signal colour, with olive #718D0B on its shadowed sides. Nothing else is lime or saturated; no red, orange or blue accents. Lighting: one large soft key light from the upper left at about 45 degrees, like diffused north-window daylight, with a gentle white bounce fill from the right; soft grounded contact shadows fall to the lower right. Camera: 100mm macro lens at f/4, eye level with the tabletop, three-quarter view. The hero object is tack sharp and the background melts into smooth, creamy blur on a seamless pale neutral sweep. Mood: calm, precise, orderly and quietly premium, like high-end editorial product photography. Strictly no people, figures, faces, hands or silhouettes. No readable text, letters, numbers, clock digits, logos, signage or user-interface graphics anywhere. No holograms, floating screens, robots with faces, dense cable tangles, carnival or circus elements, cartoon or plastic CGI look, oversaturated colour, lens flare or heavy vignette.

The lime indicator on the far corner laptop still blinks, the only lit point there. Ivory paper forms have drifted off the dead desks onto the tabletop. Acrylic chips hang in the air above the breaks, and the darkness spreads straight back toward the router. Wide 16:9 landscape frame, same layout and angle as the calm version of this scene. Photorealistic photograph of a vast handcrafted miniature landscape diorama. A wide, dim plain of dark grey paper ash stretches to a faint horizon under a low haze. Scattered across it lie giant broken frosted rings, their segments half sunk and cracked, forming broken circular ridges around the building-sized graphite router, which stands rusted at the far left, one antenna snapped. Ivory card desks lie across the plain as weathered, bleached slabs, their laptops closed and dust covered. In the midground, a slim graphite mast rig on three thin legs is planting a row of small repeater posts, each topped with a lime relay lamp, in a straight line from the router toward the far corner desk, the first three posts glowing and lighting a narrow path across the dark ground. Wide 16:9 panoramic frame. The main ruin anchors the left or centre foreground, terrain rolls back to a distant horizon on the upper third, and the lime recovery rig sits in the right midground. Surfaces carry believable imperfections: fine dust, paper grain, hairline creases, light scuffs on metal. Every object has convincing miniature scale and weight and rests firmly on its surface.
